name: linux-arm64-kvm-mte-v1
purpose: Detect and execute the fresh-hugetlb KVM_ARM_MTE_COPY_TAGS helper-domain bug in complete ARM64 KVM guest.c, then compare only patch 4.

static_analysis.command_policy: The complete guest.c was included through a one-entry database mapped from its exact successful ARM64 Kbuild command.

baseline.diagnostic: page_mte_tagged may receive page 'page' while its related folio 'folio' is known to be hugetlb

static_analysis.specificity: The separate mte-init finding remains because patch 4 intentionally does not change the tag-import ordering addressed by patches 1 and 2.

checker_policy.predicate: track the true and false successors of direct folio_test_hugetlb results
checker_policy.page_folio_relation: connect direct assignments and page_folio, compound_head, or _compound_head conversion results
checker_policy.report_condition: a related folio may be hugetlb on the CFG path reaching a base-page MTE helper
checker_policy.scope: intraprocedural source-shape analysis; not a general points-to or whole-kernel proof

runtime_control.environment: QEMU 10.2.1 TCG; virt with MTE and virtualization; max CPU; GICv3; two vCPUs; 1024 MiB; all CPUs at EL2; KVM VHE; two preallocated 2 MiB hugepages
runtime_control.request: KVM_ARM_MTE_COPY_TAGS tag read for one 4 KiB page in a fresh anonymous 2 MiB hugetlb memslot

vulnerable.failure: VM_WARN_ON_ONCE at arch/arm64/include/asm/mte.h:58 in kvm_vm_ioctl_mte_copy_tags followed by panic_on_warn

runtime_control.controlled_variables: The trigger, initramfs, kernel configuration, and QEMU command were identical; only patch 4 differed between kernels.

candidate_disposition.status: automated exact-source finding with vulnerable-panic/fixed-pass ARM64 MTE/KVM runtime confirmation; maintainer confirmation pending
candidate_disposition.confirmation_scope: runtime confirmed under QEMU TCG, not maintainer confirmed or upstream accepted

limitations: Static aliasing is intentionally limited to direct local variable and known page-to-folio conversion shapes.
A zero checker result means this narrow helper-domain path was absent, not that MTE or KVM is correct.
The runtime control uses QEMU TCG rather than physical ARM64 hardware.
The other MTE series defects remain static candidates without vulnerable-fail/fixed-pass runtime confirmation.
Linux KVM maintainer review and upstream acceptance remain pending.
interpretation: The checker reports the real vulnerable expression and becomes silent for the ternary helper selection. Independently, the vulnerable Linux kernel panics on the focused valid ioctl and the patch-4 kernel passes under identical emulated ARM64 MTE/EL2/KVM conditions. This is the project's second runtime-confirmed Linux bug, while upstream confirmation remains a separate milestone.
